policies.content:
POL-001 | Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Curriculum Rigor Evaluation: Evaluation requires selecting the most challenging coursework available within the applicant's secondary school environment, specifically Advanced Placement (AP), International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme, or dual-enrollment institutional tracks.

policies.title: Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
policies.content:
POL-002 | Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Grade Point Average (GPA) Standard: Maintenance of an unweighted GPA between 3.8 and 4.0 on a 4.0 scale is established as the baseline threshold. GPA is analyzed contextually via the High School Profile to gauge relative class rank performance.

policies.title: Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
policies.content:
POL-003 | Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Weighted vs. Unweighted Divergence: The academic screening layer prioritizes internal school rankings and absolute course rigor over inflated weighted GPAs to normalize variations across global grading systems.

policies.title: Standardized Testing Distributions
policies.content:
POL-004 | Standardized Testing Distributions
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT) Threshold: The middle 50% score band for admitted candidates resides between 1500 and 1600, with a critical focus on cross-section consistency.

policies.title: Standardized Testing Distributions
policies.content:
POL-005 | Standardized Testing Distributions
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: American College Testing (ACT) Threshold: The middle 50% score band for admitted candidates resides between 34 and 36.

policies.title: Standardized Testing Distributions
policies.content:
POL-006 | Standardized Testing Distributions
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Policy Flexibility: Under test-optional or test-blind institutional variances, quantitative weight shifts dynamically to the Academic Index calculation and external validation metrics (e.g., AP exam scores of 5).

policies.title: The Academic Index (AI) Formula
policies.content:
POL-007 | The Academic Index (AI) Formula
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: AI Definition: A numerical score ranging from 60 to 240, aggregating calculated GPA, class rank (where available), and standardized test components to create a unified academic baseline.

policies.title: The Academic Index (AI) Formula
policies.content:
POL-008 | The Academic Index (AI) Formula
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Cohort Balancing Application: Used to ensure recruited athlete cohorts and specialized institutional sub-populations remain within a statistically acceptable variance of the general student body's academic profile.

policies.title: Extracurricular Impact Tiers
policies.content:
POL-009 | Extracurricular Impact Tiers
Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES
Policy: Tier 1 (National/International Distinction): Includes elite milestones such as attending prestigious summer programs (e.g., RSI, TASP), winning national Olympiads, founding widely recognized organizations, or generating peer-reviewed academic publications.

policies.title: Extracurricular Impact Tiers
policies.content:
POL-010 | Extracurricular Impact Tiers
Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES
Policy: Tier 2 (Regional/State Leadership): High-level execution within local ecosystems, including student body presidency, state-level athletic or artistic recognition, or founding impactful local initiatives.

policies.title: Extracurricular Impact Tiers
policies.content:
POL-011 | Extracurricular Impact Tiers
Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES
Policy: Tier 3 (School/Community Engagement): Active participation in varsity sports, school clubs, or sustained local volunteerism showing reliable contribution without broad external scaling.

policies.title: Intellectual Curiosity & Institutional Contribution
policies.content:
POL-012 | Intellectual Curiosity & Institutional Contribution
Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES
Policy: Intellectual Curiosity: The candidate demonstrates self-driven pursuit of knowledge beyond standard classroom requirements, as evidenced by academic coursework, extracurricular activities, awards, and teacher recommendations.

policies.title: Intellectual Curiosity & Institutional Contribution
policies.content:
POL-013 | Intellectual Curiosity & Institutional Contribution
Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES
Policy: Institutional Contribution: The candidate's academic interests, leadership, extracurricular involvement, and community engagement are evaluated using available academic records, activities, awards, and recommendation letters.

policies.title: Recommendation Weight & Letters of Evaluation
policies.content:
POL-014 | Recommendation Weight & Letters of Evaluation
Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES
Policy: Teacher Evaluations: Requires two letters from core academic disciplines (STEM and Humanities) written by instructors who can explicitly benchmark the applicant against the top 1–2% of students in their teaching careers.

policies.title: Recommendation Weight & Letters of Evaluation
policies.content:
POL-015 | Recommendation Weight & Letters of Evaluation
Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES
Policy: Counselor Report: Provides institutional context, confirming the student's character, disciplinary standing, and relative peer standing within the graduating cohort.

policies.title: The Regional Committee Advocacy System
policies.content:
POL-016 | The Regional Committee Advocacy System
Section: SECTION 3: INSTITUTIONAL NEEDS, SELECTION COMMITTEES, & STRATEGIC HOOKS
Policy: First-Round Review: Applications are parsed by a dedicated Regional Admissions Officer who scores the file and drafts an advocacy summary based on geographic context.

policies.title: The Regional Committee Advocacy System
policies.content:
POL-017 | The Regional Committee Advocacy System
Section: SECTION 3: INSTITUTIONAL NEEDS, SELECTION COMMITTEES, & STRATEGIC HOOKS
Policy: Full Committee Debate: The Regional Officer presents the applicant's case to the full admissions committee, where a majority vote determines the final selection or rejection.

policies.title: Institutional Balancing Acts (Cohort Sculpting)
policies.content:
POL-018 | Institutional Balancing Acts (Cohort Sculpting)
Section: SECTION 3: INSTITUTIONAL NEEDS, SELECTION COMMITTEES, & STRATEGIC HOOKS
Policy: Recruited Athletes: Candidates backed by varsity athletic coaches bypass traditional yield modeling, provided they pass basic Academic Index baseline parameters.

policies.title: Institutional Balancing Acts (Cohort Sculpting)
policies.content:
POL-019 | Institutional Balancing Acts (Cohort Sculpting)
Section: SECTION 3: INSTITUTIONAL NEEDS, SELECTION COMMITTEES, & STRATEGIC HOOKS
Policy: Socioeconomic & Geographic Diversity: Deliberate institutional sculpting to represent all US states, diverse international territories, first-generation college students, and underrepresented backgrounds.

policies.title: Institutional Balancing Acts (Cohort Sculpting)
policies.content:
POL-020 | Institutional Balancing Acts (Cohort Sculpting)
Section: SECTION 3: INSTITUTIONAL NEEDS, SELECTION COMMITTEES, & STRATEGIC HOOKS
Policy: Legacy & Institutional Advancement: Policy adjustments handle considerations for children of alumni or institutional donors, though individual university policies are subject to ongoing regulatory updates.

policies.title: Institutional Balancing Acts (Cohort Sculpting)
policies.content:
POL-021 | Institutional Balancing Acts (Cohort Sculpting)
Section: SECTION 3: INSTITUTIONAL NEEDS, SELECTION COMMITTEES, & STRATEGIC HOOKS
Policy: Academic Major Distribution: Caps are placed on oversaturated majors (e.g., Computer Science, Economics) to distribute the incoming cohort evenly across all academic departments.

policies.title: Extracurricular Impact Tiers
policies.content:

policies.title: Extracurricular Impact Tiers

Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES

policies.content:

Section: SECTION 2: HOLISTIC REVIEW & QUALITATIVE RATING SCALES

Policy: Counselor Report: Provides institutional context, confirming the student's character, disciplinary standing, and relative peer standing within the graduating cohort.

policies.content:

Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Curriculum Rigor Evaluation: Evaluation requires selecting the most challenging coursework available within the applicant's secondary school environment, specifically Advanced Placement (AP), International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme, or dual-enrollment institutional tracks.

policies.title: Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
policies.content:
POL-002 | Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Grade Point Average (GPA) Standard: Maintenance of an unweighted GPA between 3.8 and 4.0 on a 4.0 scale is established as the baseline threshold. GPA is analyzed contextually via the High School Profile to gauge relative class rank performance.

policies.title: Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
policies.content:
POL-003 | Academic Rigor & Contextual GPA Evaluation
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Weighted vs. Unweighted Divergence: The academic screening layer prioritizes internal school rankings and absolute course rigor over inflated weighted GPAs to normalize variations across global grading systems.

policies.title: Standardized Testing Distributions
policies.content:

Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES

policies.title: Standardized Testing Distributions
policies.content:

Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES

policies.title: Standardized Testing Distributions
policies.content:
POL-006 | Standardized Testing Distributions
Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: Policy Flexibility: Under test-optional or test-blind institutional variances, quantitative weight shifts dynamically to the Academic Index calculation and external validation metrics (e.g., AP exam scores of 5).

policies.content:

Section: SECTION 1: ACADEMIC SCREENING FRAMEWORK & QUANTITATIVE BASELINES
Policy: AI Definition: A numerical score ranging from 60 to 240, aggregating calculated GPA, class rank (where available), and standardized test components to create a unified academic baseline.
